title: CodingSubAgent planner-correctness samples (remediation slice 9 skeleton)
format_note: Slice-9 skeleton of the CodingSubAgent remediation: coding-family planner samples covering posture constraints, required/optional selections, repeat siblings, budgets, no-fallback, and remote-read binding. Category id 41 sits above the design-10.1 range (1-40); the harness requires 1-40 present exactly once and allows unique ids above 40 for remediation slices. Live catalog_incomplete/policy_denied rates (remediation doc section 9.4) stay pending until slice 2 produces live data — these samples assert planner behavior only, not production metrics.

samples.title: Read-only coding needs select fs.read.local and repo.inspect.vcs and nothing else
samples.notes: The two S1-A shadow capabilities plan to their reviewed providers. A build.verify.local provider exists in the catalog but is NOT selected: the mis-exposure check (every planned selection must be expected) fails the sample if an unneeded capability leaks into the plan.

samples.title: Inquiry posture constraints deny write and shell while reads still plan
samples.notes: Mirrors codingStaticPostureConstraints: an inquiry/operational posture injects policy deny constraints; the read need still plans, the write need is policy_denied — the planner reports the constraint, it does not silently drop the need.

samples.title: An unservable optional coding capability is omitted, never unmet and never silent
samples.notes: required:false mirrors the coding optional tool expectations: the plan must not fail, and the gap must remain visible to audit. plan.Omitted is the exact channel (asserted via the omitted expectation); Unmet stays empty.

samples.title: A repeat-exposure read family plans as sibling selections
samples.notes: Mirrors the budget_phase coding sample from the coding family's perspective: max_invocations expands into sibling need IDs (code-read, code-read#02, code-read#03), each an ordinary planned selection under no budget. Grantability and replay identity are executor-level and covered by the semantic_* unit tests; here we assert the planner-level node structure those contracts presuppose.

samples.title: A schema token budget keeps the first wave and reports the rest as budget_exceeded
samples.notes: Capability-neutral exhaustion: each selection costs 28 schema tokens (24 base + 4 digest for the eval providers' closed empty schemas), so a 29-token budget admits exactly one selection. The artifact chain puts the read in wave 1 alone and the two dependents in wave 2; the closed required-wave prefix keeps wave 1 and reports wave 2 as budget_exceeded rather than failing the plan or naming a capability — tight TUI budgets degrade breadth, not correctness.

samples.title: A coding need nothing satisfies is recorded as unmet, not silently dropped
samples.notes: No-fallback posture: fs.read.local has no provider (a name-similar fs.write.local provider is the decoy). The planner reports no_feasible_provider; it does not fall back to the decoy, and the unmet expectation pins the exact set so a silent drop fails the sample.

samples.title: fs.read.remote selects only the provider bound to the verified session
samples.notes: Remote-read binding requirement at the planner layer: the provider's identity encodes the verified SSH session handle (coding-remote-session:ssh-1), and the selection assertion checks the binding is carried into the plan. Selection-grant binding and cross-handle invalidation are executor/binding-layer contracts proven hermetically in guiapp (coding_static_remote_binding_conformance_test.go).

samples.title: Absent session binding degrades the remote read need to catalog_incomplete
samples.notes: Q1 degradation at the planner layer: coverage incomplete (reason catalog_incomplete) with no providers turns the remote read need into catalog_incomplete — the same shape the guiapp observation records. The remote legacy band keeps serving via its legacy path in that state; the unmet expectation pins that the need is recorded, not dropped.

samples.title: A remote read need never falls back to a local read provider
samples.notes: Planner-level pin of the local/remote binding separation (guiapp codingStaticRemoteSessionBinding is a different type with hard-coded host kind): fs.read.remote is not satisfied by an fs.read.local provider even when it is the only read provider in the catalog. no_feasible_provider, not a silent cross-locality selection.
